facts.statement: The skull of Gargoyleosaurus is 29 centimeters long, broad and triangular, with shields that take the shape of horns at the back.
facts.quote: El cráneo de 29 centímetros de largo es amplio y triangular, con los escudos que toman la forma de cuernos en la parte posterior

facts.statement: The body armor of Gargoyleosaurus consists of thin-walled oval cones with at least two elongated dorsal spines projecting from each shoulder.
facts.quote: La armadura corporal se compone de conos ovales de paredes delgadas, con por lo menos dos espinas dorsales alargadas proyectando de cada hombro.

facts.statement: The seven premaxillary teeth of Gargoyleosaurus are conical and resemble those of early stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Los siete dientes premaxilares son cónicos y se asemejan en algo a los de los estegosáuridos tempranos

facts.statement: The genus name Gargoyleosaurus is derived from the English word gargoyle, referring to its grotesque appearance.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del inglés gargoyle, gárgola, una referencia a la apariencia grotesca.

facts.statement: The species name honors the discoverers and is a contraction of the first syllables of their surnames.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a los descubridores y es una contracción de las primeras sílabas de sus apellidos.

facts.statement: The holotype of Gargoyleosaurus was discovered in 1995 at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality in Albany County, Wyoming, within the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in 1995 at the Bone Cabin Quarry West locality, in Albany County, Wyoming in exposures of the Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages) Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: The type species Gargoyleosaurus parkpinorum was described by Ken Carpenter and colleagues in 1998.
facts.quote: The type species, G. parkpinorum (originally G. parkpini) was described by Ken Carpenter et al. in 1998.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Gargoyleosaurus parkpinorum was collected by Western Paleontology Labs in 1995 and is held in the Denver Museum of Nature and Science.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Gargoyleosaurus parkpinorum was collected by Western Paleontology Labs in 1995 and is currently held in the collections of the Denver Museum of Nature and Science, Denver, Colorado.

facts.statement: In 1996, Jeff Parker and Tyler Pinegar, employees of Western Paleontology Labs, found the skeleton of an ankylosaur at the Bone Cabin Quarry West site in Albany County, Wyoming, in the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: En 1996, Jeff Parker y Tyler Pinegar, empleados de los laboratorios comerciales paleontológicos occidentales, encontraron el esqueleto de un anquilosauriano en el sitio de Bone Cabin Quarry West en el condado de Albany, Wyoming en la Formación Morrison que expone sedimentos del Jurásico superior.

facts.statement: In 1998, Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward named and described the type species Gargoyleosaurus parkpini.
facts.quote: En 1998, Kenneth Carpenter , Clifford Miles y Karen Cloward nombraron y describieron el tipo de Gargoyleosaurus parkpini.

facts.statement: Gargoyleosaurus was present in stratigraphic zone 2 of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Gargoyleosaurus was present in stratigraphic zone 2 of the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: Gargoyleosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 152 to 145 million years ago, in the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 152 y 145 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense y Titoniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Soto-Acuña and colleagues in 2021 recovered Gargoyleosaurus as a nodosaurid.
facts.quote: In contrast, a phylogenetic analysis by Soto-Acuña and colleagues in 2021 recovered Gargoyleosaurus as a nodosaurid.

facts.statement: In 2005, Carpenter placed the species in the Polacanthidae, viewing it as a basal group of Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: En 2005, sin embargo, Carpenter colocó la especie en el Polacanthidae, visto por él como un grupo básico de Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: A 2011 analysis by Richard Campbell Thompson shows a fairly basal position of Gargoyleosaurus in Nodosauridae, as a relative of Polacanthus.
facts.quote: Un análisis de Richard Campbell Thompson de 2011 muestra una posición bastante básica de Gargoyleosaurus en Nodosauridae, como familiar de Polacanthus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Gargoyleosaurus belongs to Ankylosauridae or Nodosauridae, as previous studies supporting Ankylosauridae only used skull data while distinctive Polacanthinae features appear in the postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: Estos estudios sin embargo, solamente han utilizado el cráneo, mientras que muchas de las características distintivas de la subfamilia Polacanthinae se presentan en el esqueleto postcranial.

facts.statement: The genus Gargoyleosaurus was described by Carpenter and colleagues in 1998.
facts.quote: Carpenter et al. 1998

facts.statement: Gargoyleosaurus belongs to the family Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: Gargoyleosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.

facts.statement: Gargoyleosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
